title: A split torus action without invariant tangent vectors forces split unipotence
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and smoothness and connectedness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Let $H$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type, and let $S\simeq\mathbf G_{m,k}^r$, $r\geq0$, act on $H$ by group-scheme automorphisms. Here $\mathbf G_m$ and $\mathbf G_a$ are [def-sc-gm-ga]; an action is a morphism $S\times_kH\to H$ satisfying the identity and associativity laws and preserving multiplication in $H$. Let $\mathfrak h$ be the tangent space of $H$ at the identity [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], with the differentiated $S$-action. Assume $\mathfrak h^S=0$, where the invariant subspace consists of vectors fixed after every commutative $k$-algebra extension by every point of $S$. Then $H$ is split unipotent: there is a finite series $H=H_0\supset H_1\supset\cdots\supset H_m=1$ of smooth geometrically connected closed $k$-subgroups, each normal in its predecessor, whose fppf quotient sheaves $H_i/H_{i+1}$ are represented by $\mathbf G_a$. Fppf quotient means sheafification of the right-coset functor for flat finitely presented jointly surjective coverings. In particular $H$ has a faithful finite-dimensional matrix representation in which every geometric point $h$ satisfies $(h-I)^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. The action is an algebraic torus action, not merely an action of $S(k)$ or its Lie algebra; no perfection or characteristic restriction on $k$ is imposed, and $H=1$ and $r=0$ are allowed. The unipotence and represented-quotient conventions agree with [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure].

source.place: Proposition 16.63, printed p.347; Proposition 16.62 and Theorem 16.58, printed pp.345,347; split-series convention in Section 16g. This general automorphism-action criterion is the input used in the proof of Proposition 17.60, printed p.372.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-representation-weight-decomposition] to the differentiated action on $\mathfrak h$. Its zero-character space is precisely the invariant subspace in the hypothesis, so every occurring character is nonzero. After choosing $S\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$, write the finitely many characters as nonzero integer vectors $b$. Choose $v\in\mathbf Z^r$ with $b\cdot v\ne0$ for all of them: for $r>0$ take $v=(1,M,\ldots,M^{r-1})$ with the integer $M$ avoiding the finitely many roots of the nonzero polynomials $\sum b_iM^{i-1}$. The resulting cocharacter $\lambda(t)=(t^{v_1},\ldots,t^{v_r})$ gives no zero weight on $\mathfrak h$. If the weight set is empty take the trivial cocharacter, also when $r=0$. The direct-sum description shows after every field extension that $\mathfrak h^S=0$ still holds; tangent base extension here is the dual of base extension of the finite-dimensional cotangent space at the rational identity.

source.place: Proposition 16.62, first paragraph, p.347; integer cocharacter choice supplied explicitly by the worker.

proof.text: Over $F=\bar k$ form $J=H_F\rtimes S_F$ with underlying affine scheme $H_F\times_FS_F$ and multiplication $(h,s)(h',s')=(h\,a(s,h'),ss')$. The action axioms give a group scheme and make $H_F$ a closed normal subgroup; projection has section $s\mapsto(1,s)$. Both factors are smooth and geometrically connected. Smoothness of this product follows by base change and composition [lem-pc-proper-base-change, lem-trf-smooth-composition]; connectedness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components]. Thus $J$ is a smooth connected affine algebraic group, with no reductivity assumption.

source.place: Proposition 16.62, first paragraph, p.347: semidirect product and maximal tori.

proof.text: Choose a maximal torus $T$ of $J$ containing $S_F$: enlarge $S_F$ until the dimension is maximal, which terminates since torus ranks are bounded by $\dim J$ and a proper inclusion of tori raises rank. By [lem-sfb-normal-subgroup-maximal-torus-intersection], $K=((H_F\cap T)_{\mathrm{red}})^\circ$ is a maximal torus of $H_F$. Since $S_F\subseteq T$ and $T$ is commutative, $S_F$ fixes $K$ pointwise. The tangent map of its closed immersion is injective (apply its surjective coordinate-ring map to dual-number points), so $\operatorname{Lie}K\subseteq(\mathfrak h_F)^{S_F}=0$. A torus of rank $d$ has tangent dimension $d$, directly from $F[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_d^{\pm1}]$ at $z_i=1$; hence $K=1$. Every torus lies in a maximal one by the same rank argument, and maximal tori of $H_F$ are conjugate [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy]. Therefore $H_F$ has no nontrivial torus. A nontrivial $k$-torus would remain such over $F$, so $H$ has none. Apply [lem-sfb-torus-free-implies-unipotent-arbitrary-field] over $k$ to obtain a faithful upper-unitriangular closed representation of $H$. In particular the matrix clause of the item already follows.

source.place: Proposition 16.62, first paragraph, p.347; its unipotence argument, using maximal-torus intersection to avoid any descent assumption on a chosen torus.

proof.text: Restrict the action to $\lambda$ from step 1. By [lem-sfb-gm-action-attracting-subgroup-big-cell] the subgroups $U_-$ and $U_+$ are smooth geometrically connected affine $k$-groups, and multiplication is a dense open immersion $U_-\times_kU_+\to H$. The $\lambda$-action on $\operatorname{Lie}U_+$ has strictly positive integer weights. On $U_-$ use $t\mapsto\lambda(t^{-1})$, which negates its strictly negative weights. Apply [lem-sfb-positive-weight-affine-space-arbitrary-field] to the rational fixed identity in each group. This gives $k$-scheme isomorphisms $U_\pm\simeq\mathbf A_k^{d_\pm}$, including a point for dimension zero, and hence a dense open immersion $\mathbf A_k^N\to H$ with $N=d_-+d_+$. Restrict to the dense open $D(T_1\cdots T_N)\simeq(\mathbf G_m)^N$ of $\mathbf A^N$; its image remains dense in $H$. Algebraically its coordinate map is the injection for the dense affine chart followed by $k[T_1,\ldots,T_N]\hookrightarrow k[T_1^{\pm1},\ldots,T_N^{\pm1}]$. For $N=0$ use the identity localization.

source.place: Theorem 13.33 and Theorem 13.41, pp.265-270; corrected replacement for the invalid strict-definiteness inference in Proposition 16.62 and the proof of Proposition 16.63, p.347.

proof.text: The representation of step 3 proves that $H$ is unipotent over $k$, so [lem-sfb-smooth-unipotent-solvable] gives solvability over this same field, without assuming it perfect. Apply [lem-sfb-rosenlicht-split-solvable-criterion] to the dominant scheme morphism $(\mathbf G_m)^N\to H$ from step 4. Its unipotent clause gives a finite series of smooth geometrically connected closed $k$-subgroups, normal in their predecessors, with represented fppf quotients $\mathbf G_a$. This is exactly the required series. The faithful representation from step 3 supplies the additional matrix assertion; in an $n$-dimensional upper-unitriangular representation $(h-I)^n=0$. If $H=1$ the series may be empty and a one-dimensional trivial representation is faithful. No step uses rational-point weights in place of algebraic characters.

source.place: Theorem 16.58, p.345, and the split-unipotent conclusion of Proposition 16.63, p.347.

proof_origin.place: Propositions 16.62-16.63, p.347, with an explicit correction of the false strict-definiteness assertion; Theorems 13.33,13.41 and16.58 supply the replacement.
